content:
What's supposed to happen during the account setup is that, using OAuth2 for authorization as (I believe) Yahoo requires, a web browser window should pop up and prompt you through entering your credentials and choosing whether or not to link to Yahoo's address book and calendar.

The only version of Ubuntu I have available is 26.04. I just added a Yahoo account to Thunderbird 160 and it all went as I described above. But I used to have the earlier version and did not have a problem with this. I would say that your Ubuntu is confused about how to deal with the authentication web page.

Some things that might help...

- Make sure cookies are enabled in Thunderbird (see <Settings | Privacy & Security | Web Content | Accept cookies from sites>.)

- Remove any existing cookies from Yahoo in Thunderbird (see <Settings | Privacy & Security | Web Content | Show Cookies button>.)

- Remove any existing Yahoo entries in Saved Passwords (see <Settings | Privacy & Security | Passwords | View Saved Passwords>.)

- Try changing the default web browser to something else temporarily. You can change it back after a successful authorization. Or, confirm to the OS that your current browser is truly the default.

Then restart Thunderbird and try setting up the account again. Hopefully the authorization will complete successfully. Please let us know how it goes.

content: To clean up an IMAP folder in Thunderbird, start by unsubscribing from it so it no longer appears in your folder list. Right-click the folder → Subscribe → uncheck it.If you later decide you want the folder permanently gone, log into the account through the provider’s webmail and delete it there. That removes it from the server.Folders shown in italics are typically “no-select” folders. They can’t hold messages themselves; they only serve as containers for other folders. Some people use them as organizational headers. If you’re dealing with a greyed-out italic “ghost” folder that won’t behave normally, try this: Rename the folder by adding a letter or number at the beginning of its name. Rename it back to the original name. Completely quit Thunderbird and relaunch it. Check whether the folder now appears as a regular folder. If it does, unsubscribe from it so it disappears from the view .

Are your ios email clients using POP ? If yes, POP account folders do not synchronise with server. They access the server and simply download new mail from server Inbox to Pop account Inbox. They are completely independent of server.

That means the issue is not with Thunderbird as it is an imap account and it is updating and synchronsing with server.
